title: Resurrecting Label Propagation for Graphs with Heterophily and Label Noise

problem.claim: Label noise can substantially degrade the generalization ability of deep neural networks, and graph models are particularly susceptible because they use both node features and graph topology through message passing.

gap.claim: Existing graph methods for label noise generally assume homophily and smoothly distributed labels, making them inadequate for graphs with substantial or dominant heterophily.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph message passing increases susceptibility to label noise because graph models combine node features and topology.
Only a small number of studies address label noise on graphs.
Existing approaches assume homophily and smooth label distributions.
Real-world heterophilous graphs expose the inadequacy of those assumptions.

source_observation.claim: Methods for graph label noise should account for graph heterophily rather than assume homophily.

interpretation.claim: A method's robustness may depend on whether its label-smoothing assumptions match the graph's structural regime.

application.claim: When evaluating graph learning under label noise, include graphs with varying or dominant heterophily.

exception.claim: The supplied units do not establish how such methods should behave across specific heterophily levels.

unknowns: The proposed method or contribution is not stated.
No datasets, experimental setup, results, or quantitative findings are supplied.
The paper's specific treatment of heterophily and label noise is not described.
